verdict.rationale: Supermemory documents a genuine self-hosting path: 'runs on your own hardware' as a single self-contained binary with local graph engine, local embeddings, and local LLM so 'data never leaves the building,' with no Docker/database/config required to boot it. This directly satisfies an AI-native user's desire to self-host the core memory engine rather than only use the hosted SaaS. Missing for 10: independent/hands-on verification that self-hosted deployment actually works as documented (all evidence is first-party docs, no community reports of successful self-hosting).
